name: Oregon

agency.name: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI)

rates2026.note: Baker, Coos, Crook, Curry, Douglas, Gilliam, Grant, Harney, Jefferson, Klamath, Lake, Malheur, Morrow, Sherman, Umatilla, Union, Wallowa, Wheeler; July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027

tipped.note: Tip credits are illegal: tipped workers get the full regional minimum ($16.80 Portland metro, $15.55 standard, $14.55 non-urban).

minWage.other: Minors get the same minimum wage as adults. Rates adjust every July 1 to CPI (Portland = standard + $1.25; non-urban = standard - $1.00).

source.quote: For July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027, those rates are: $16.80 per hour - Portland metro ... $15.55 per hour - Standard $14.55 per hour - Non-urban

overtime.exemptSalaryNote: Oregon's salary test is tied to the regional minimum wage and stays below the federal $684/week.

source.quote: If you work more than 40 hours in one week, you must receive overtime pay of 1.5 times your regular pay rate.

sickLeave.accrual: 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (or 40 hours front-loaded)
sickLeave.capNote: Up to 40 hours per year; paid if the employer has 10+ Oregon employees (6+ with a Portland location), otherwise protected but unpaid. Usable after 90 days of employment.
sickLeave.employerThreshold: all employers (paid at 10+ employees, 6+ in Portland)

source.quote: Employees earn at least 1 hour of protected sick time for every 30 hours of work, up to 40 hours per year.

familyLeave.name: Paid Leave Oregon
familyLeave.replacement: Sliding scale based on base-year wages and the state average weekly wage (SAWW): up to 100% of wages for lower earners, capped at 120% of SAWW
familyLeave.medicalLeave: Included in the same 12 weeks (own serious health condition); up to 2 extra weeks for pregnancy-related limitations (14 total).
familyLeave.stateUnpaidLaw: Oregon Family Leave Act (OFLA), employers with 25+ employees: unpaid job-protected leave for pregnancy disability (up to 12 extra weeks), sick child leave and bereavement leave.

source.quote: Employees can take up to 12 weeks paid leave in a 52-week period ... If pregnant, in some situations, an employee may be able to take up to 2 more weeks for a total of 14 weeks.

finalPay.fired: by the end of the next business day
finalPay.quit: with 48+ hours' notice: on the last day of work; with less notice: within 5 business days or the next regular payday, whichever comes first
finalPay.ptoNote: Vacation pay is not required; an established policy or agreement to pay out accrued vacation must be honored.

source.quote: If you are let go or fired, your final paycheck is due by the end of the next business day.

ptoSource.quote: Your employer is required to honor any established policy or agreement relating to the payment of benefits such as accrued vacation or severance pay upon termination.

breaks.meal: 30-minute unpaid meal period for work periods of 6 hours or more (relieved of all duties)
breaks.rest: Paid 10-minute rest break for each 4-hour segment (two per 8-hour shift)

source.quote: For each 8-hour work period you get these breaks free from work responsibilities: Two 10 minute paid rest breaks One 30 minute unpaid meal break

notes.text: Oregon has three regional minimum wages (Portland metro, standard, non-urban) that change every July 1; inside the Portland urban growth boundary the Portland rate applies.

source.quote: If your work location is within the urban growth boundary , you must be paid at least the "Portland Metro" rate.

notes.text: Tip credits are illegal in Oregon: tips cannot be counted toward the minimum wage.

source.quote: Tips are separate and cannot be counted as wages. Tip credits are illegal in Oregon.

notes.text: A late final paycheck can cost the employer penalty wages of 8 times the regular rate per day, for up to 30 days.

source.quote: a penalty wage equal to eight times the employee's regular rate of wage for each day that final wages go unpaid up to 30 days
